propositions: Plan review and code review currently make independent discovery decisions through partially separate registry, routing, runner, checkpoint, and failure paths, leading to policy-ownership defects where one gate can disable built-ins, omit project criteria, ignore applicability, or confuse failed work for successful checkpoints.

Implement unified discovery architecture where both gates share one immutable effective-policy snapshot containing built-ins, project LLM/DET criteria, routing, prompts, and posture, with gate-owned strategies and a shared typed executor that enforces budget, cancellation, and success-only checkpointing without choosing applicability or deciding verdicts.

Project code-review LLM criteria must require non-empty repository-relative globs (migrate `project.review-phase-boundaries` from `[]` to `["**"]`), while positive explicit `usd_budget` values remain authoritative for both gates and omission preserves existing plan-review budget policy.

Add `rebar review-plan --retry` to retry only the latest completed `INDETERMINATE` review with retryable missing calls, reusing content-identical successes and granting each retry a fresh attempt budget, documented across all canonical operator surfaces.

Preserve code-review sequential execution, topology, and base-reviewer contracts while preserving plan-review chunking, concurrency, cache warming, checkpointing, and cancellation; move to digest-complete success-only checkpoint namespace with persisted versioned discovery trace for audit and diagnostics.

Workflow editor must separate editable Authored Workflow from read-only Effective Policy, enforce non-empty code-review glob lists with `["**"]` remedy, and use expand-contract migration without duplicate model calls to compare legacy and new projections before approving deltas.
